purpose: Operational causal workflow knowledge for the DeepUplift Agent.

principles.title: Causal workflow before model chasing
principles.guidance: Start with data design, overlap, leakage, balance, and identification assumptions before ranking models.

principles.title: Ranking quality must be stress-tested
principles.guidance: Use QINI/AUUC together with Top-K policy value, calibration, segment stability, and bootstrap confidence intervals.

principles.title: Uplift is a policy problem
principles.guidance: Translate uplift scores into targeting thresholds, expected value, and risks before recommending deployment.

principles.title: Growth uplift must align offline ranking with online delivery
principles.guidance: For push, SMS, RTA, and resource-slot campaigns, optimize and validate Top-K recall, QINI, policy value, and score calibration together.

diagnostic_rules.message: Treatment assignment looks close to randomized from observed features. Simple meta-learners and neural baselines are reasonable first candidates.
Treatment assignment is predictable from covariates, so observational selection bias is likely. Prefer doubly robust or orthogonal learners and inspect overlap.
Weak overlap is present. Estimates for poorly covered users can be unstable; consider trimming, overlap-weighted metrics, and conservative policy thresholds.
Treatment/control sizes are imbalanced. X-Learner and DR/R-style learners are often better baselines than plain T-Learner.
assumptions: minority group has enough positive outcomes for evaluation

diagnostic_rules.message: Some covariates differ substantially between treatment groups. Balance-aware representation models and orthogonal learners should be included.
assumptions: observed covariates are sufficient to adjust selection

diagnostic_rules.message: The current binary uplift workflow is not enough. Use multi-treatment learners and compare action-specific policy value.
Continuous treatment requires dose-response modeling, not binary QINI/AUUC alone.

evaluation_rules.message: If uplift buckets are not monotonic or calibration error is high, use the score for ranking cautiously and validate with holdout or bootstrap.
Model comparison should prefer stable lower confidence bounds over single-point QINI/AUUC wins.
Segment analysis is useful for surfacing HTE, but small segment counts should be treated as hypotheses rather than deployment rules.
Distill black-box uplift rankings into shallow segment rules for business review, then validate support and holdout stability before deployment.
A deployment recommendation should include contact cost, conversion value, and the best targeting threshold.
Before deployment, a model should beat random-score and permuted-treatment null checks; otherwise treat the ranking as exploratory.
If policy value or QINI collapses after common-support trimming, deployment should be limited to well-overlapped users or delayed for more data.
A multi-treatment run should be validated by action-specific uplift, recommended action mix, and Top-K recommended-policy export before use.
Multi-treatment policy recommendations need action-level overlap diagnostics and policy-value uncertainty, especially when some actions are rare.
Compare multi-treatment T- and DR-learners by incremental policy-value lower bound, action overlap, and recommended action mix rather than by a single point estimate.
When the business decision is Top-K targeting, PAV/isotonic calibration can make uplift scores more reliable as a monotone ranking signal.
On synthetic or benchmark data with known treatment effects, use Oracle Top-K recall to test whether the model actually finds high-uplift users.
When delivery, DM, online, or business-score columns exist, compare uplift Top-K against that ranking to detect offline-online mismatch before rollout.
Before exporting a targeting list, compare scoring population features against training profiles to catch SSB and deployment-distribution drift.

risks: can underfit heterogeneous effects because treatment is only another feature
SLearnerGBM.explanation: S-Learner is a fast sanity-check baseline. Use it to verify the pipeline and compare against richer CATE learners.

risks: can smooth away small uplift effects
less direct extrapolation control
SLearnerRF.explanation: S-Learner with a random forest outcome model is a robust nonlinear baseline.

risks: can be unstable when one treatment group is small
TLearnerGBM.explanation: T-Learner trains separate outcome models for treatment and control, then subtracts predictions.

risks: two separate forests can amplify noise when groups are small
TLearnerRF.explanation: T-Learner with forest outcome models is useful when response surfaces are nonlinear.

risks: depends on high-quality first-stage outcome models
XLearnerGBM.explanation: X-Learner imputes treatment effects using counterfactual outcome models, then blends effect models using propensity.

risks: propensity blending can be unreliable under weak overlap
XLearnerForest.explanation: X-Learner with a forest effect stage is a strong practical baseline for unequal treatment/control sizes.

risks: poor overlap can still cause high-variance pseudo outcomes
DRLearnerGBM.explanation: DR-Learner combines outcome and propensity models so one nuisance model can partially protect the effect estimate.

risks: DR pseudo outcomes can be noisy under weak overlap
DRLearnerForest.explanation: A forest final stage learns nonlinear structure in doubly robust pseudo outcomes.

risks: requires useful outcome and propensity nuisance models
RLearnerGBM.explanation: R-Learner residualizes outcome and treatment before learning CATE, reducing nuisance-model error leakage into the final effect model.

risks: residual signal can be weak when propensity is near 0 or 1
RLearnerForest.explanation: R-Learner with a forest final stage is useful when orthogonal residuals have nonlinear interactions.

risks: current implementation is a lightweight adapter, not a full cross-fit EconML DML implementation
OrthogonalDMLGBM.explanation: OrthogonalDML-style learning uses residualized signals to make effect learning less sensitive to first-stage model errors.

risks: current implementation is local forest final-stage logic, not full generalized random forest inference
OrthogonalRandomForest.explanation: Orthogonal Random Forest style learning combines residualization with a forest CATE stage.

risks: current adapter is forest-style rather than a full generalized random forest
CausalForest.explanation: CausalForest-style models are useful when interactions are nonlinear and segment-level heterogeneity matters.

risks: can be high variance outside randomized or well-overlapped data
TransformedOutcomeGBM.explanation: Transformed Outcome models learn a direct uplift pseudo outcome and are useful as a quick experiment baseline.

risks: high variance if treatment assignment is confounded
TransformedOutcomeForest.explanation: Forest transformed outcome learning captures nonlinear uplift in randomized-like data.

risks: unstable when propensity is close to 0 or 1
IPWLearnerGBM.explanation: IPW learning estimates uplift from inverse-propensity weighted pseudo outcomes.

risks: inherits IPW high variance under weak overlap
IPWForest.explanation: IPWForest uses a forest final stage on inverse-propensity weighted pseudo outcomes.

risks: requires reliable propensity estimates
does not solve unobserved confounding
DomainAdaptationLearner.explanation: Domain Adaptation Learner reweights outcome models to reduce observed distribution shift between groups.

risks: plain T-learner can be unstable when treatment/control sizes are very imbalanced
TLearnerLightGBM.explanation: TLearnerLightGBM trains separate LightGBM outcome models for treatment and control and is a strong industrial ranking baseline.

risks: depends on useful first-stage counterfactual outcome models and propensity blending
XLearnerLightGBM.explanation: XLearnerLightGBM combines LightGBM counterfactual outcome models with LightGBM effect stages.

risks: weak overlap can still create high-variance pseudo effects
DRLearnerLightGBM.explanation: DRLearnerLightGBM uses LightGBM for outcome and effect stages around a doubly robust pseudo-effect signal.

risks: requires enough residual signal after outcome and propensity nuisance modeling
RLearnerLightGBM.explanation: RLearnerLightGBM residualizes outcome and treatment, then learns the final CATE surface with LightGBM.

risks: calibration should be validated on holdout and with bootstrap before deployment
GGBMUpliftLightGBM.explanation: GGBMUpliftLightGBM combines a DR pseudo-effect signal, LightGBM effect stage, and isotonic/PAV calibration.

risks: plain two-model uplift can be noisy with small treatment/control cells
SkLiftTwoModelsLightGBM.explanation: SkLiftTwoModelsLightGBM wraps the official scikit-uplift TwoModels interface and returns unified y0/y1/uplift outputs.

risks: single-model treatment interactions can underfit heterogeneous effects if interactions are weakly represented
SkLiftSoloInteractionLightGBM.explanation: SkLiftSoloInteractionLightGBM uses scikit-uplift SoloModel with explicit treatment-feature interactions.

risks: classification-only and sensitive to confounded treatment assignment
SkLiftClassTransformationLightGBM.explanation: SkLiftClassTransformationLightGBM wraps the official scikit-uplift class-variable transformation learner.

risks: propensity estimates can add variance under weak overlap
SkLiftTransformedOutcomeLightGBM.explanation: SkLiftTransformedOutcomeLightGBM wraps scikit-uplift ClassTransformationReg with a LightGBM effect stage.

risks: requires optional catboost installation and local runtime validation
GGBMUpliftCatBoost.explanation: GGBMUpliftCatBoost is the CatBoost version of the calibrated DR pseudo-effect ranking learner.

risks: isotonic calibration can overfit small holdouts
still requires overlap and nuisance-model checks
GGBMUpliftGBM.explanation: GGBMUpliftGBM uses a doubly robust pseudo-effect signal, a GBM effect stage, and PAV/isotonic calibration for monotone uplift ranking.

risks: calibration quality depends on enough treated/control support across the score range
PAVCalibratedDRLearnerGBM.explanation: PAVCalibratedDRLearnerGBM fits a DR learner and then learns a monotone mapping from raw uplift scores to DR pseudo effects.

risks: R-learner residual signal can be noisy under weak overlap
PAVCalibratedRLearnerGBM.explanation: PAVCalibratedRLearnerGBM calibrates R-learner uplift scores with an isotonic/PAV mapping.

risks: forest variance and calibration variance should be checked with bootstrap
PAVCalibratedCausalForest.explanation: PAVCalibratedCausalForest combines forest-style CATE learning with monotone uplift calibration.

risks: requires binary outcome
can be biased when treatment assignment is strongly confounded
ClassVariableTransformGBM.explanation: ClassVariableTransformGBM transforms binary response into a class-variable uplift target and maps it back to treatment-effect scores.

risks: forest score variance should be checked with calibration and Top-K validation
ClassVariableTransformForest.explanation: ClassVariableTransformForest is a nonlinear CVT uplift baseline for randomized-like binary conversion data.

risks: experimental local adapter; validate against transformed outcome and DR/R learners before relying on it
PAVCalibratedClassVariableTransformGBM.explanation: PAVCalibratedClassVariableTransformGBM applies isotonic calibration to a CVT uplift score to improve monotone ranking behavior.

risks: does not explicitly balance treatment/control representations
TarNet.explanation: TarNet learns shared representations with separate treatment/control outcome heads.

risks: representation balancing does not fix unobserved confounding
CFRNet.explanation: CFRNet extends TarNet by encouraging balanced representations across treatment groups.

risks: can overfit on small tabular datasets without careful validation
DragonNet.explanation: DragonNet jointly learns outcome heads and treatment assignment, which helps expose selection structure.

risks: needs enough data to learn interactions
EFIN.explanation: EFIN emphasizes explicit feature interactions for uplift modeling.

risks: classification-only in current registry
DESCN.explanation: DESCN/ESX targets entire-space uplift estimation for binary response tasks.

EconMLGRFCausalForest.explanation: EconML GRF CausalForest provides a mature generalized random forest style estimator.

CausalMLUpliftRandomForest.explanation: CausalML UpliftRandomForestClassifier is useful for direct classification uplift benchmarks.

CausalMLCausalRandomForest.explanation: CausalML CausalRandomForestRegressor is the optional path toward multi-treatment tree/forest support.

risks: single-model treatment encoding can miss subtle heterogeneity
CausalMLSLearnerLightGBM.explanation: CausalMLSLearnerLightGBM wraps CausalML BaseS with a LightGBM outcome learner.

risks: requires CausalML Python 3.11 runtime validation
CausalMLTLearnerLightGBM.explanation: CausalMLTLearnerLightGBM wraps CausalML BaseT with a LightGBM outcome learner.

risks: depends on reliable propensity and counterfactual outcome stages
CausalMLXLearnerLightGBM.explanation: CausalMLXLearnerLightGBM wraps CausalML BaseX with a LightGBM learner.

risks: requires enough residual treatment variation after nuisance modeling
CausalMLRLearnerLightGBM.explanation: CausalMLRLearnerLightGBM wraps CausalML BaseR with a LightGBM learner.

risks: IPW policy value depends on overlap for every action
separate outcome models can be noisy for rare actions
MultiTLearnerGBM.explanation: MultiTLearnerGBM trains one outcome model per action and recommends the action with the highest predicted outcome.

risks: rare actions can overfit
policy estimates need action-level overlap checks
MultiTLearnerRF.explanation: MultiTLearnerRF is a forest-based multi-action T-Learner for nonlinear action-specific response surfaces.

risks: DR pseudo effects can still be unstable under weak action overlap
requires useful outcome and propensity models
MultiDRLearnerGBM.explanation: MultiDRLearnerGBM learns action-vs-control doubly robust pseudo effects with a GBM final stage.

risks: rare actions can produce high-variance pseudo effects
requires action-level overlap checks
MultiDRLearnerRF.explanation: MultiDRLearnerRF uses forest effect models for nonlinear doubly robust action uplift.

risks: requires observed support across the dose grid
current implementation is a practical S-learner baseline rather than full VCNet
DoseResponseGBM.explanation: DoseResponseGBM learns an outcome model over features plus continuous dose and scores a grid of possible doses for each user.

risks: can be noisy outside observed dose support
does not yet provide DRNet/VCNet targeted regularization
DoseResponseRF.explanation: DoseResponseRF uses a forest outcome model over features plus continuous dose to estimate individual dose-response curves.

risks: rules summarize the fitted model rather than proving causal identification
small leaves can be unstable without bootstrap or holdout checks
CausalDistillationTree.explanation: CausalDistillationTree distills a trained uplift model's scores into a shallow decision tree so humans can review high-uplift segments.

research_frontier.business_signal: Large-scale marketing uplift benchmarks still favor comparing S/T/X learners and causal forests on QINI, cumulative gain, Top-K capture, and uncertainty rather than trusting one model family.
research_frontier.agent_action: Keep Compare as the default workflow and add LightGBM/EconML adapters when dependencies are available.

research_frontier.business_signal: Black-box CATE models need stable, readable subgroup explanations for deployment review.
research_frontier.agent_action: Generate Causal Distillation Segments after every binary uplift run and validate them with support, holdout uplift, and bootstrap.

research_frontier.business_signal: Imbalanced randomized uplift data can make transformed-outcome learners fragile; class-flipping style corrections are a candidate next adapter.
research_frontier.agent_action: Use ClassVariableTransformGBM and PAVCalibratedClassVariableTransformGBM as local classification baselines, then add exact class-flipping correction only with reproducible validation.

research_frontier.business_signal: Growth scenarios often have multiple incentives and multiple response tasks, so action-specific uplift should not be reduced to binary treatment.
research_frontier.agent_action: Extend the current Multi-Treatment page toward multi-task outcomes after binary/multi-action scoring is stable.

research_frontier.business_signal: Prior-fitted causal transformers may automate estimator choice and uncertainty on small or medium observational datasets.
research_frontier.agent_action: Treat as optional external research adapter; do not block local deterministic training on it.

research_frontier.business_signal: Repeated touchpoints need longitudinal HTE with carryover and post-treatment bias handling, beyond static uplift.
research_frontier.agent_action: Add a sequence/longitudinal data design first, then consider Transformer-enabled recursive R-learner adapters.

model_selection_dilemma.title: In Search of Insights, Not Magic Bullets: Towards Demystification of the Model Selection Dilemma in Heterogeneous Treatment Effects
model_selection_dilemma.signal: No single HTE model dominates; model choice should depend on data design and validation.

multi_valued_meta_learners.title: Comparison of meta-learners for estimating multi-valued treatment heterogeneous effects
multi_valued_meta_learners.signal: Multi-treatment settings need action-specific learners and evaluation, not binary uplift shortcuts.

causal_isotonic_calibration.title: Causal isotonic calibration for heterogeneous treatment effects
causal_isotonic_calibration.signal: Calibration matters for using CATE scores as policy rankings.

r_learning_inverse_variance.title: The Connection Between R-Learning and Inverse-Variance Weighting for Estimation of Heterogeneous Treatment Effects
r_learning_inverse_variance.signal: R-learning and pseudo-outcome weighting are central for robust HTE estimation.

covariate_balancing_ipm.title: Covariate balancing using the integral probability metric for causal inference
covariate_balancing_ipm.signal: Balance diagnostics and IPM-style representation checks help detect treatment/control mismatch.

confounding_bounds.title: Bounds on the conditional and average treatment effect with unobserved confounding factors
confounding_bounds.signal: Unobserved confounding can invalidate point estimates; use sensitivity/bounds thinking.

hte_surfacing.title: A Systematic Paradigm for Detecting, Surfacing, and Characterizing Heterogeneous Treatment Effects
hte_surfacing.signal: Subgroup discovery should be framed as hypothesis surfacing and validated.

continuous_treatment_foundation.title: Causal Foundation Models with Continuous Treatments
continuous_treatment_foundation.signal: Continuous treatment requires dose-response workflows and cannot be reduced to binary uplift.

survival_hte.title: SurvHTE-Bench: A Benchmark for Heterogeneous Treatment Effect Estimation in Survival Analysis
survival_hte.signal: Time-to-event outcomes need survival-specific HTE metrics and censoring assumptions.

dowhy_dr.title: DoWhy v0.14: Python 3.13 support and a new doubly robust estimator
dowhy_dr.signal: Doubly robust estimation and refutation workflows are becoming standard platform capabilities.

selection_bias.title: Towards a holistic understanding of Selection Bias for Causal Effect Identification
selection_bias.signal: Selection bias should be diagnosed before model selection and deployment.

task_specific_experimental_design.title: Task-specific experimental design for treatment effect estimation
task_specific_experimental_design.signal: Experiment design should be aligned with the downstream effect-estimation task.

adaptive_sampling_ads.title: Optimal Data Integration and Adaptive Sampling for Efficient Treatment Effect Estimation
adaptive_sampling_ads.signal: Advertising treatment-effect work should connect estimation to campaign selection and value.

bootstrap_confidence.title: Bootstrap aggregation and confidence measures to improve time series causal discovery
bootstrap_confidence.signal: Confidence measures are necessary for deciding whether a model win is stable.

causal_rule_subgroups.title: CURLS: Causal Rule Learning for Subgroups with Significant Treatment Effect
causal_rule_subgroups.signal: Subgroup rules should be surfaced with significance and support checks.

upliftbench_2026.title: A Large-Scale Empirical Comparison of Meta-Learners and Causal Forests for Heterogeneous Treatment Effect Estimation in Marketing Uplift Modeling
upliftbench_2026.signal: Industrial marketing uplift should benchmark meta-learners and causal forests with QINI, cumulative gain, Top-K capture, and uncertainty.

terra_longitudinal_2025.title: TERRA: A Transformer-Enabled Recursive R-learner for Longitudinal Heterogeneous Treatment Effect Estimation
terra_longitudinal_2025.signal: Time-varying treatment workflows need sequence-aware effect estimation that handles carryover and post-treatment bias.

causal_distillation_trees_2025.title: Distilling heterogeneous treatment effects: Stable subgroup estimation in causal inference
causal_distillation_trees_2025.signal: Black-box HTE estimates can be distilled into stable, interpretable subgroup rules.

class_flipping_uplift_2024.title: Class flipping for uplift modeling and Heterogeneous Treatment Effect estimation on imbalanced RCT data
class_flipping_uplift_2024.signal: Imbalanced randomized uplift data needs corrections that avoid distorting treatment effects.

mtmt_user_growth_2024.title: Multi-Treatment Multi-Task Uplift Modeling for Enhancing User Growth
mtmt_user_growth_2024.signal: Growth workflows often require multi-treatment and multi-task uplift rather than single binary response modeling.

causalpfn_2025.title: CausalPFN: Amortized Causal Effect Estimation via In-Context Learning
causalpfn_2025.signal: Prior-fitted causal transformers are a candidate path for automated estimator choice and calibrated uncertainty.

deployment_policy.title: DeepUplift Agent policy-value principle
deployment_policy.signal: Uplift scores must be converted into decisions, thresholds, and economic value.

business_growth_resume.title: Growth uplift business resume notes
business_growth_resume.signal: Growth uplift production systems emphasize SSB mitigation, GGBM-style scalable effect learning, PAV/isotonic calibration, QINI, Top-K recall, and online/offline alignment.
